name: nvidia_gpu_exporter
description: Prometheus exporter for NVIDIA GPUs. It runs `nvidia-smi` and parses its output, so it works wherever `nvidia-smi` works: Linux, Windows, macOS, containers, VMs. There is also an experimental backend that reads the driver library (NVML) directly.

warnings_fixed_justification: Lint is part of the required CI check, so a warning blocks the merge. There are zero warnings in the tree.

know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer builds infrastructure software professionally. The exporter follows least privilege: the packages run it as a dedicated unprivileged user, the container image is distroless, and no GPU is reserved. The container image runs as a non-root uid and the chart's default security contexts satisfy the restricted Pod Security Standard. It fails safe: a failed collection publishes no data instead of stale data. The attack surface is small: a read-only subprocess and an HTTP endpoint, with optional TLS and basic auth via the Prometheus exporter toolkit. Written up in https://github.com/utkuozdemir/nvidia_gpu_exporter/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md
know_common_errors_justification: The relevant error classes for this software, and what is done about them. Command injection via the configurable `nvidia-smi` command: no shell is involved, the exporter splits the arguments itself. Untrusted parser input from any driver or wrapper: every parser has a fuzz target, and a panic is treated as a bug. Resource exhaustion from a stuck subprocess: collection timeout and a scrape concurrency limit. Supply chain: actions pinned by commit, images pinned by digest, signed releases.
crypto_published_justification: The only cryptography is TLS on the metrics endpoint, optional, via the Prometheus exporter toolkit. It uses Go's `crypto/tls`.
crypto_call_justification: The project implements no cryptography. TLS comes from the Go standard library and bcrypt from `golang.org/x/crypto`, both via the Prometheus exporter toolkit.
crypto_floss_justification: Go standard library and `golang.org/x/crypto`. Both FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: The exporter generates no keys. It is a TLS server only, and the operator supplies the certificate and key in the web config file. The negotiated key exchange follows Go's defaults (ECDHE, P-256 and up, AES-128 and up), and the minimum TLS version and cipher suites can be restricted in that file.
crypto_working_justification: Go's TLS defaults. No broken algorithms in there.
crypto_pfs_justification: Go's TLS uses ECDHE key exchange by default, and always on TLS 1.3.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The optional basic auth on the metrics endpoint stores only bcrypt hashes (Prometheus exporter toolkit web config).
delivery_mitm_justification: All downloads go over https. Additionally, the checksums file, the container images and the Helm chart of every release are signed keyless with cosign (releases before this carry a GPG signature on the checksums file instead), and the classic chart repository carries GPG provenance: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/nvidia_gpu_exporter/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md#verifying-what-you-downloaded
delivery_unsigned_justification: The checksums file is served over https and has a keyless cosign signature bundle (`checksums.txt.sigstore.json`).

vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No vulnerability so far. The policy for when one comes: prioritized by severity, fix ships in a release, then an advisory: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/nvidia_gpu_exporter/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md

GitHub CodeQL scans the repository through the default setup, on pull requests and weekly: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/nvidia_gpu_exporter/security/code-scanning
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: gosec via golangci-lint, and CodeQL, on every change.

static_analysis_often_justification: On every push and pull request.
dynamic_analysis_justification: The test suite runs under the Go race detector in CI on every change, so every release is preceded by it. On top of that, Go fuzz targets cover the parsers and the metric name derivation (`task test:fuzz`), run during development rather than as a formal release step, and their seed corpora are replayed in every normal test run: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/nvidia_gpu_exporter/blob/main/AGENTS.md
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Go. The optional NVML flavor uses a cgo binding that is a dependency.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Every fuzz target asserts a property, not just the absence of a panic: a parsed table is safe to index, a transformed value is finite, a derived metric name is registrable. Tests run with `-race`.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No vulnerability found by dynamic analysis so far. Crashes found by fuzzing are fixed and their inputs go into the seed corpus, which the normal test run replays, so they stay fixed.
dco_justification: Contributed code carries a DCO sign-off, and the contribution guide requires `git commit -s` for pull requests: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/nvidia_gpu_exporter/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md. Honest limits: the automated dependency commits from Renovate carry no sign-off, and no bot enforces the trailer.

sites_password_security_justification: The project sites are GitHub, Docker Hub, grafana.com and Artifact Hub. All manage their own authentication, the project stores no passwords itself.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Only the latest release is maintained, and upgrading is replacing the binary, the package or the image tag. The project does not rename established metrics or flags. Metric names derive from the headers the driver returns, so a driver upgrade can rename a metric, which is outside the project's control and documented. Breaking changes are called out in the release notes.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability resolved in the last 12 months.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/nvidia_gpu_exporter/blob/main/.github/SECURITY.md: private report, first response within two weeks, fix in the next release, then an advisory with credit.
coding_standards_justification: gofmt and golangci-lint with all linters, shfmt and shellcheck for shell, markdownlint for docs. The contribution guide says so: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/nvidia_gpu_exporter/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: `task lint` runs all of it in containers at pinned versions, and the CI build fails on any finding.
build_standard_variables_justification: The Go toolchain honors `GOFLAGS`, and the cgo nvml flavor honors `CC`, `CGO_CFLAGS` and `CGO_LDFLAGS`. The static flavor involves no C compiler.
build_preserve_debug_justification: `go build` from source keeps the debug information. Only the release binaries are stripped (`-s -w`) to keep the downloads small.
build_non_recursive_justification: One Go module, one build graph. `go build ./...` resolves the dependencies itself.
build_repeatable_justification: The release builds use `-trimpath`. The commit time is the timestamp of the binaries, of every archive and package entry, and of the packages themselves, and the rpm build host is fixed. Every archive entry has a fixed owner and mode, because an archive entry otherwise records the builder's uid, user name and umask. The toolchain and every module version are pinned in `go.mod` and `go.sum`. A CI workflow builds the release files on two runners on every change and fails on any difference, and the release workflow rebuilds every release from scratch on a second runner and compares it with the published checksums. Checked on 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-03: builds by two different users on two different systems gave byte-identical checksums for every static artifact, and v1.15.1 rebuilt from a fresh clone on another machine matched the published checksums. The cgo flavor additionally depends on the build host's C toolchain, so it reproduces only on a matching builder. Releases before v1.15.1 were not reproducible across machines: v1.15.0's archives recorded the builder's user, and earlier releases had no reproducibility work at all.
installation_common_justification: deb and rpm packages, winget, Scoop, container images, a Helm chart, and the Windows service has its own `install` and `uninstall` commands: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/nvidia_gpu_exporter/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md
installation_standard_variables_justific: The packages install to `/usr/bin` and `/usr/lib/systemd/system`. The archives are a single binary you put where you want. `go install` honors `GOBIN` and `GOPATH`.
installation_development_quick_justifica: `git clone`, `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`. The linters run in containers via `task lint`, at the versions CI uses. No GPU needed: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/nvidia_gpu_exporter/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md
dependency_monitoring_justification: Renovate updates dependencies continuously, and GitHub Dependabot alerts are enabled for the repository.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Go modules, nothing vendored. A dependency is updated by bumping it in `go.mod`, which Renovate does on its own.
interfaces_current_justification: staticcheck, part of the golangci-lint set, flags deprecated APIs, and the build fails on it.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: On every push and pull request. The result is the check on the commit: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/nvidia_gpu_exporter/blob/main/.github/workflows/build.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: Bug fixes come with a test. For parser and driver-output bugs that is usually a recorded capture, which the integration suite then replays forever.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Statement coverage is 91% measured locally with `go test -coverpkg=./... ./...` on 2026-08-30, and 87% on Codecov for the main branch (measured on Linux CI). An earlier 62% figure was a stale pre-branch-rename record on Codecov, not this code base.
implement_secure_design_justification: Least privilege, fail safe, small attack surface, no shell, fuzzed parsers. How each one is applied and checked: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/nvidia_gpu_exporter/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The TLS cipher suites, curves and minimum version are configurable in the web config file (Prometheus exporter toolkit).
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The TLS private key is its own file, referenced by path from the web config file. Basic auth is stored only as bcrypt hashes, inside that config file, which exists solely for the web serving configuration. Nothing sensitive is on the command line or in the environment.
crypto_used_network_justification: TLS 1.2+ is supported for the one network interface the exporter has, but plain HTTP is the default, which is the Prometheus exporter convention. Enabling TLS is one config file away: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/nvidia_gpu_exporter/blob/main/docs/CONFIGURE.md
crypto_tls12_justification: The exporter toolkit defaults to TLS 1.2. The web config file can raise the minimum to 1.3, or lower it, so 1.2 is the default, not a hard floor.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: The exporter is a TLS server only. It makes no outbound TLS connections, so there is no certificate to verify on its side. Client certificates can be required and are then verified.
signed_releases_justification: The checksums file carries a keyless cosign signature bundle, which covers every built artifact: binaries, archives and packages. The images and the chart are signed keyless with cosign too, so no stored key is involved in any of these. The one GPG signature left is the Helm chart's provenance file for the classic repository, because Helm verifies nothing else. Release tags are signed since v1.15.0, and the release workflow refuses a tag GitHub does not verify. How to verify: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/nvidia_gpu_exporter/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md#verifying-what-you-downloaded. Honest limits: the auto-generated GitHub source archives are not covered, tags before v1.15.0 are unsigned, and the chart provenance is signed in the release workflow with a GPG key stored as a CI secret.
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are signed since v1.15.0 (2026-09-02). The release task creates a signed tag from the tip of main. The release workflow refuses a tag GitHub does not show as verified, and a tag that does not name the release or does not point at the commit being built. Release tags are immutable by ruleset. Tags before v1.15.0 are unsigned. https://github.com/utkuozdemir/nvidia_gpu_exporter/tags
input_validation_justification: Flags are validated at startup and an impossible combination is an error, not a silent ignore. Unknown query fields fail loudly. Parser output is checked before use: unrecognized state values are skipped and logged, a derived metric name that is empty or collides is dropped. All of it fuzzed.
hardening_justification: Static binary with no cgo in the default build. Distroless image with no shell, running as a non-root uid. The packages run the service as a dedicated user. The chart drops all capabilities and disallows privilege escalation by default. Collection timeout and scrape concurrency limit bound resource use.
assurance_case_justification: https://github.com/utkuozdemir/nvidia_gpu_exporter/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md: security requirements, trust boundaries, threats with their mitigations, and how each is checked.
